title: Seeing Josephine Baker in Liza before sailing
summary: Howard saw Josephine Baker as end girl in the all-colored show Liza at the Daly's Theater in New York, then found her famous in Paris.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you play any place in this country or did you just go to Europe?

No, we played every place but New York. The only place we didn't play was waiting for the passports. Oh, you played all over the East Coast? Now look, it was the first and the only time that I seen Josephine Baker, she was in that show Liza at the Davidson Theater in New York.

And by the time we got to Paris, she was as big as this room in Paris already. Mm-hmm. You know? Farley's Brigitte. Mm-hmm. And that's where we left her. She was the end girl in that show Liza. The end girl? Yeah. We went to see that show and we sailed the next day.
Was that George Gershwin's show, Liza?
I don't know. No. No, it was da da da da da da da. No, that wasn't it. That's a regression of the term. It was another title. I mean another song.
Another Liza. They were doing, what did this Jack do to this Charleston on? Babelina.
You remember that song, don't you? Yes. Babelina. They were doing those numbers in there. I could be wrong, I don't know.
Was this Liza an all-color show too?
That's right, 1923, the Davidson Theater. You can look that up.
Was Florence, wasn't that show? Oh no. No. Before her time.
No, it wasn't before her time. No. Oh no.
No? No. She had just left to play, even when we were playing in the Empire Theater in Leicester Square. It was a block off in London.
